will depend on its ability to deliver on
the commitments already made and to
demonstrate that multilateralism
can make a meaningful difference in the
lives of people. Mr. President, the
Secretary General's UN8 initiative to

better equipped for the future is

honorable President uh shared with us

duplication,
strengthen accountability,
retire mandates that no longer serve
their purpose, and direct scarce
resources towards measurable results. At
the same time, reform should preserve
the organization's ability to deliver
across its three pillars of peace and
security, development, and human rights,
and should not make it more difficult
for small states to participate
meaningfully in its work.
Mr. President,
as the UN begins its search for his next
secretary general, I take this
opportunity to convey our deepest
appreciation to his excellency Antonio
Gutierrez, whose term as the ninth

Secretary General Gutirez will be well

strain and for advancing important

posed by nuclear weapons. We also

position
in senior UN uh leadership positions and
his efforts to bring super intelligence
and the risks posed by nuclear weapons
more firmly into the international
agenda. Mr. President, as I close, I say
that Trinidad's longstanding commitment
to multilateralism and the United
Nations has been anchored in delivering
results and adding value to the lives of

forward, it is important for us all to
remember that trust must be earned and
built on the principles of mutual
respect and cooperation. The Republic of
Trinidad and Tobago is prepared to play
its role and part to rebuild a United
Nations that delivers for all. Mr.
President, I thank you and may God
continue to bless each and every one of
you. Thank you very much.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the prime minister of the Republic
